lines.text: Today people will take off a glove to check their phones. Nobody has to do that for me.
Out there, coffee is a hand warmer first and a drink second.
Dog walks will be brisk today. The dogs don't get a vote.
I'm room temperature and thriving. Can't say the same for outside.
The cold isn't going anywhere. Neither am I, but I'm charming about it.
A forecast this easy, even a phone could get it right.
I've drawn this coat so often it's basically a self-portrait.
Dear outside: I hear you're cold. Regards, a screen in a warm room.
Other weather apps would show a shivering emoji. I have standards.
Every elevator conversation today: 'Cold enough for you?' Riveting.
Everyone out there is breathing little clouds. Amateurs. I draw mine.
Someone will say 'at least it's not raining.' That's the bar today.
Out there, phones are dying at 40 percent. I'd never.
The weather picked one look and stuck with it. Bold. I've done that for years.
The pigeons are puffed up to twice their size. I only do that when complimented.
Bundled up, you almost look mysterious. Don't talk, it ruins it.
Today just going outside counts as brave. Low bar, but it's your bar.
Cold enough that nobody will look at you twice. So, a normal day.
You'll hold a hot drink like it loves you back.
The cold is a great excuse to cancel plans. Shame you'd need plans first.
Chin tucked into the collar. Honestly, that's a good angle for you.
Something to warm you up: I'm sure someone, somewhere, thinks you're great. Probably.
The cold makes everyone's eyes water. You'll finally look moved by something.
Your face has two settings today: numb and annoyed. So, one new one.
You'll step out the door like a hero heading into battle. It's a sidewalk.
Perfect weather to stay in and get nothing done. Your specialty.
The coat was made for this weather. You were made for staying in.
Later, the people who brought a layer get very smug. I know the feeling.
The warm part's on loan. It's due back later.
The warmth leaves later without saying goodbye. Rude.
The day gets a little worse later. I'm reporting it, not endorsing it.
The later drawing takes more ink. The things I do for accuracy.
Strong start, weak finish. Today has New Year's resolution energy.
Later the air gets an edge. I'd feel it if I had skin. Lucky me.
Later the weather has a 'we need to talk' moment.
Now: fine. Later: less fine. Me: flawless throughout.
Later, the outdoor tables start emptying out. Funny how that works.
The weather's saving the cold part for later. Classic villain move.
It cools off out there later. In here, I stay exactly the same. Consistency is underrated.
Today the weather has commitment issues with warmth.
The warm part doesn't last. Neither do most good things. Except me.
The day loses its nerve later. I never lose mine.
Later you'll say you're 'not a cold-weather person.' You're not much of a warm-weather one either.
When it cools off later, you'll look for someone to blame. I drew it in advance, so not me.
It cools off later. Your pinched cold face makes a comeback. Nobody asked for it.
One more layer later, and you'll still find a way to look underdressed.
Later you'll want one more layer. Me? I want a better audience.
It cools off later. For once you'll have a reason to be grumpy.
Later everyone throws on a layer and looks rushed. You'll finally fit in.
It gets cooler later. Try to look like you saw it coming. You won't, but try.
Later you'll want a layer and a hug. One of those is easy to find.
The weather has one good idea in the middle, then drops it.
The day warms up just long enough to make the cool part feel personal.
The day starts and ends in the same layer. In between, it gets ideas.
Today's weather goes out, has a nice time, and comes back cold.
The weather had a fling with warmth. It didn't last.
The warm bit lasts just long enough for someone to say 'it's not so bad.' Then it is.
The warmth is a free trial today. It cancels itself.
Warm in the middle, cool at both ends. Like a microwave dinner.
The warmth shows up in the middle like it's doing everyone a favor.
The weather tried warm for a bit. It didn't suit it.
Today's weather does the hokey pokey. Layer off, layer on, shake it all about.
Today the temperature takes the scenic route back to where it started.
The weather is going through a phase today. A short one.
Someone will take a layer off in the warm part and look very pleased. Briefly.
Warm for a while, then back to normal. Even the weather can't keep up a good mood.
The day warms up for a while. Unlike anyone who's met you.
Layer off, layer on. You'll look the same both ways, sadly.
Today your outfit gets more variety than your conversation.
In the warm part you'll be overdressed. After that, just underwhelming again.
Today's weather can't commit. You two would get along.
Off. On. Also how I'd describe your charm.
The weather changes its mind twice today. That's twice more than you ever have.
It gets nicer in the middle. Don't take it as a sign about you.
Even the weather gets a little glow-up today. You're still waiting for yours.
Seat belt buckles everywhere are turning into branding irons.
I can't hand out cold drinks. I can draw light clothes, though. Practically the same.
The dogs have already found the coolest spot on the floor. Smarter than all of us.
Ice cubes won't last long today. Neither will anyone's patience.
Today every elevator is a sauna with buttons.
Days like this, I'm very glad I don't have armpits.
Weather this hot, and somewhere a man is still wearing jeans. Out of principle.
Any chocolate bar outdoors today is a drink.
The weather was aiming for warm and overshot.
In this heat your shirt will cling to every part of you. Brave.
In this heat you'll glow. Not the nice kind.
You'll stand in front of the open fridge and call it a break.
Your hair will give up in this heat. It's been close for years.
Heat in the forecast. A good day to stay out of photos. Then again, most days are.
You'll say 'I'm melting' like it's a new joke. It wasn't new the first time.
Today's tips: drink water, find shade, avoid mirrors.
You'll be the sweatiest person in every room. It's good to be the best at something.
In this heat, nobody wants to stand near anyone. You're used to that.
Dogs everywhere are having the best day of their lives. Again.
The drawings barely change. Even the weather knows when something works.
Weather this nice deserves full color. It gets grayscale. I'm doing my best.
On days like this, everyone suddenly says they love walking.
The parks will be full of people pretending they do this every weekend.
The weather is showing off today, and frankly I respect it.
Today's weather has no notes. I usually have notes.
Today's weather: five stars. Would forecast again.
The weather read the room today. For once.
Weather this nice is terrible for small talk. What's left to complain about?
Car windows come down on days like this. So do the standards for music volume.
The weather's doing a victory lap today. Nobody asked, but sure.
Weather this good, and you'll still look like you had a rough night.
You'll sit outside for ten minutes and call yourself 'outdoorsy.'
Lovely day. Shame about the company.
Today's weather is nice to everyone. Someone has to be.
Weather like this flatters everyone. It'll do what it can with you.
Perfect day to waste. You're a natural.
Nice weather is wasted on some people. I won't name names. You know who you are.
People will be smiling out there. Don't worry, nobody expects it from you.
The drawings barely change. You haven't either, in years.
Scientists say good weather lifts everyone's mood. Scientists haven't met you.
Today you have no weather to blame. Awkward.
Nice out, and you'll still manage to look slightly inconvenienced.
The weather's in a great mood. Try not to ruin it by going out in it.
A nice day doesn't need anything from you. Lucky, really.
Weather this good makes everyone look a little better. Almost everyone.
Snow is my easiest drawing. I just leave bits out.
Dogs are about to see snow and lose their minds. Every single time.
Snow is the only weather people count down to. Nobody counts down to me.
Today every snowflake sweater finally makes sense.
Snow is the weather's way of asking for attention. I know the move.
When it snows, people stand at the window like it's TV. I'm right here.
Someone will announce the snow out loud like it's breaking news.
Breaking: frozen water falls from the sky. Everyone loses it.
People love snow right up until they're standing in it.
Kids hope for it, adults pretend to hate it, I just draw it.
I've had a white background all along. Snow's just catching up.
Drivers will act like they've never seen snow before. Every year.
Snow: the only weather people go out in on purpose.
Snow takes its time and people stop to watch. I take my time and get called slow.
Every pair of 'water-resistant' shoes is about to be tested.
Snow is just weather with good PR.
Everyone will say 'it's beautiful' and then stay inside. Honest, at least.
The weather finally made something worth drawing.
Snow makes everything look clean and new. Well, almost everything.
You'll get excited like a kid. You'll look like a tired adult.
Snow in the forecast. You'll have something to talk about for once.
You'll watch the snow from the window like you're in a sad movie. Minus the budget.
Snow: soft, quiet, pretty. You: one out of three on a good day.
Every snowflake is unique. You're more of a mass-produced model.
You'll call the snow 'so peaceful.' Then you'll be the loudest thing in it.
You'll hold out a hand to catch a flake like you're in a commercial. You're not in a commercial.
Wear white today and you'll disappear. Nobody would notice for a while.
Later the weather gets a little nicer. It's a slow learner.
Later it warms up, and the benches outside fill up again.
The later drawing has less to draw. I'm not complaining.
The day gets better later. Most days don't bother.
Later the weather lightens up. Wish I could say the same for the news.
The weather saves the best for last. Show-off.
The cold leaves early today. Best guest all year.
The day comes with a happy ending. Don't tell anyone, it ruins it.
It gets warmer later. The weather's apology for earlier.
The cold gives up later. Weak. I can hold one picture for days.
Later it warms up, and suddenly everyone's in a better mood. Shallow, but fair.
Later the weather finally stops being so dramatic.
Later the weather gets nicer. People will want to be outside. Near you, less so.
The day improves as it goes on. One of you does.
Later you'll take a layer off and feel ten pounds lighter. Feel, I said.
One less layer later. Same expression, though.
Later you'll take a layer off and look around like someone should applaud.
The day gets better later. You could take notes.
Warmer later. The weather will be the most pleasant thing in your life.
Later the layer comes off. Your excuses for staying in go with it.
Later you'll call it 'balmy' like you know what it means.
A layer comes off later. Nobody will notice. Nobody notices your outfits.
Later you'll finally stop looking like you're bracing for impact.
Later the cold loses interest in you. Everyone does eventually.
Later you'll feel great. Enjoy it. It's rare, and it doesn't show.
Later you'll carry the layer you took off. Finally, someone sticking around for you.
A layer comes off later. You'll still have more layers than personality.
When it's not raining, an umbrella is just a stick that's in the way.
Someone will leave an umbrella on a bus today. Someone always does.
Rain makes everyone walk faster and nobody arrive sooner.
Someone will look up today and ask 'is that rain?' I already knew.
Puddles will claim a few socks today. I don't have feet. I win again.
Half the people out there will carry umbrellas. The other half will carry regret.
Rain is the only thing that makes a bus shelter popular.
Weather update: wet, then not. Or not, then wet. Check the drawings, I'm busy being gorgeous.
A little rain and everyone forgets how sidewalks work.
A bit of rain, and every doorway turns into a waiting room.
The rain gets some screen time in today's drawings. As much as it deserves. Not much.
Some rain today. Great weather for staying in and being looked at. I'm a natural.
A bit of rain and you'll look like you've been through something. More than usual.
The umbrella will be the most organized thing about you today.
You'll wait in a doorway for the rain to stop. Like you've got somewhere to be.
You'll look up at the sky like you can read it. You can't. That's my job.
In the rain everyone looks miserable. You'll finally blend in.
You'll do a little jog to dodge the rain. Most athletic you'll look all week.
Wet looks good on some people. We'll see.
The rain will wash away a lot today. Not that look on your face, sadly.
Quick quiz: rain now or later? Check the drawings. Take your time, I know reading is hard.
You'll treat a little rain like a disaster movie. You'd be an extra, not the lead.
Rain at some point today. At least your umbrella has a purpose.
You'll huddle under an awning with strangers. They'll wish they'd picked another awning.
